comments.text: Noisy storm last night. If there was a tornado warning, we didn't hear it. I did hear howling wind and sideways rain. Peeked outside and the trees are still standing. Hey everyone, My community got hit really fucking hard yesterday by a pretty devastating tornado. Don't worry about me; my house, my specific neighborhood didnt get hit all that bad. My sister and her neighborhood got literally destroyed; her house is still standing, she is safe and her cats too. Many people aren't as lucky. We don't know really what all the damage really is, how many people got hurt, if anyone has passed away from this. Yesterday different neighborhoods were blockaded by police because everything was all over the damn place. Nobody could go in or out. The power went out in many neighborhoods, some places have power but some still dont. In the neighborhood my sister lives in the water is undrinkable and without power you cant boil the water. That specific neighborhood doesn't know anything really what is going on from local government because the city and county is not getting the proper information to the people properly because the power is out and therefor internet and cell towers are not working well. I and my community will organize and mobilize a response to clean up and take care of our people. The organization I work with will be networking with the people and organizations out in the more devastated locations. I will look for some donation links for some mutual aid groups besides mine. If anyone wants to donate to my mutual aid network send me a dm and ill send the link to you. I will be very busy for the next however long this will take to recover. We will get through this. In solidarity, Stag

We got absolutely hammered by rain tonight. Roads turned into rivers, parking lots became lakes, and a few people apparently looked at floodwater and thought, “My car can handle that.” Local flooding was everywhere, emergency crews were busy, and parts of town looked like they were auditioning for a disaster movie. Thankfully our house made it through with no damage. Sometimes Mother Nature likes to remind us who’s actually running the show.

Hey everyone, The people of the Greater Fox Valley region of Wisconsin got hit hard by a devastating tornado through our residential areas today. The city of Menasha, the city hit the hardest, has been cut off by police, nobody in, nobody out. Houses were destroyed, businesses were leveled, vehicles of all kinds were thrown all around. Trees are knocked over and powerlines are on the ground. The power is out all throughout the valley. The water is bad to drink, do not drink the tap water. No information is going to people that need it. Police have issued a curfew from 10pm tonight to 5am tomorrow. Many services are out of order such as power, gas, internet, and other services. Nobody inside menasha really knows what is going on over there because information is not being put out efficiently by city and county officials. We will continue to update everyone with what is going on as soon as we get information. - In Solidarity, OVN
